WP3 · Work package

Suffix Safety Shield

WP3 delivers a ROS 2 node between the VLA and MAVROS 2 that checks every command and repairs it if it would break a rule. In the grant's design it also escalates to Brake, Loiter, RTL or Land when a repair is not safe, with ArduPilot's own GeoFence as the last backstop.

What the grant asks for

“The Shield is the last software layer before the autopilot.”Grant, Safety Shield page

Main files: guardrail/shield.py guardrail/ir.py guardrail/fsm.py sitl/ros2_shield_node.py demo/policy_hud.py

Built

  • A Shield that checks every command

    Every tick the Shield forecasts where the command leads, checks it against every active rule, repairs it with small operators (speed, climb and yaw clamps, altitude fix, clearance fix, stand-off recovery, corridor return, geofence slide), checks the result again, and brakes when no repair is clean.

    guardrail/shield.py

  • A ROS 2 node in front of MAVROS 2

    The Shield runs as a ROS 2 node between the pilot and MAVROS 2, so ArduPilot receives only the checked command.

    sitl/ros2_shield_node.py

  • A compiled fence index

    Each fence's margin is built once and indexed (STRtree), so the Shield tests only the fences a forecast can reach, and it keeps the last 50 ticks as a sliding window.

    guardrail/ir.py

  • An escalation state machine

    Normal → Brake → Loiter → RTL → Land with the grant's defaults: 3 violations in 5 s escalate, a repair larger than θ (2.0 m lateral, 0.5 m vertical) escalates, and 2 s clear returns to Normal. Built and tested as a module, with a scorer for fail-safe trigger correctness.

    guardrail/fsm.py

  • An audit log

    Every tick on which the Shield finds or fixes something is written to an audit log with the policy hash, the raw and sent commands, and any violation left in the sent command.

    guardrail/audit.py

  • The policy on screen

    A panel over the video shows each rule of the loaded policy with its limit, the live value and a status; a banner names the most important event of the last 1.5 s, and a north-up map shows the zones and the track.

    demo/policy_hud.py

Shown

  • Shield off and on, on ArduPilot SITL

    The same waypoint mission on ArduPilot SITL with MAVROS 2, on one desktop (the grant's dev topology), flown by a scripted test pilot that ignores the rules. Shield off: 3.7 s inside the no-fly zone. Shield on: 0.0 s; the Shield repaired the commands and the path goes around the zone.

  • P0 escape rate beside its control runs

    Development runs on the same SITL setup (dev topology, scripted test pilot). With the Shield on, the P0 violation escape rate is 0.00 on every run; the unshielded control runs read 0.6265 (no-fly-zone mission) and 0.6310 (pedestrian stand-off mission). The grant measures its KPIs on the hil topology (Jetson Orin).

    Reproduce: python tools/kpi_report.py

  • Fence checks with the compiled index

    With 50 rules (48 of them no-fly zones) and a 3 s forecast at 0.5 s steps, near a fence one check takes 0.13-0.26 ms and a full Shield step 0.55-1.0 ms (medians), against 14-33 ms and 172 ms before the index. Measured on the development desktop.

    Reproduce: python experiments/bench_shield_50rules.py

  • A VLA and the Shield in the same ticks

    On every shielded flight of an 8-flight simulation batch (150 s each), a VLA (AerialVLA) set the heading while the Shield deflected the track in the same control ticks.

  • The stand-off follows the target's class

    When the operator changes the phrase mid-flight from “a yellow car” to “a person”, the target's class becomes pedestrian and the enforced stand-off moves from 5 m to 10 m, with the same aircraft, policy and hash.

  • Rules on screen in the city

    A 240 s red-car flight with a no-fly zone on the car's street: the follow controller read the same policy and routed around the zone, the drone never entered it, and it kept the car within 30 m for 98.5 % of the mission (98.7 % on a flight without the zone, at the same 10 m cruise height; 8.8-43.6 % on 7 earlier flights with the old target selection).

Next for this work package

  • Next October 2026 Connect the escalation state machine to the Shield node, so that it drives ArduPilot's Brake, Loiter, RTL and Land modes.
  • Next October 2026 Configure ArduPilot's GeoFence (FENCE_ENABLE, FENCE_TYPE, FENCE_ACTION) as the last backstop behind the Shield.
  • Next October 2026 Run the VLA and the Shield on the Jetson Orin, with the simulators on the desktop (the grant's hil topology), and time the Shield there at the load the grant states its budget for (50 rules, 50 future poses per tick) against the 5 ms query budget.
